title: Ashar Travel
summary: My travel site, with a running map and list of every country I've visited. Updated after each trip.
notes: After a trip I tell AI which countries to add, and it updates the data and redeploys. The October 2026 Eastern Europe trip added five countries in one pass.

title: Slack backup to Drive
summary: Every week, new messages from my Slack workspace, threads included, are saved to a fresh Google Doc. API keys get redacted along the way.
notes: The design is append-only: each run writes one new doc covering only messages since the last run, and the doc's title holds the cutoff timestamp, so a missed week loses nothing. After uploading, Claude checks the doc against a manifest of every message it collected and discards its own doc if anything is missing. I moved to this after an earlier version that rewrote one big doc silently corrupted it.

title: The Birthday Haul
summary: Sixty birthday freebies and discounts from restaurants, coffee shops and stores, searchable and sortable by how long each reward lasts.
notes: Built from my own birthday redemptions. It's a single HTML file with no build step: filter by category, search, and sort by redemption window, with tips on signing up early.

title: Startup Knowledge
summary: A knowledge base on building a startup: guides on fundamentals, funding, product and team, plus case studies, frameworks and checklists.
notes: Generated with AI as a structured reference I can come back to: 12 guides, 6 case studies, 10 frameworks and 20+ checklists, organized by topic.

title: Knicks Central
summary: A Knicks game-night page with the live score, Eastern Conference standings and the team's stat leaders in one place. Demo data.
notes: Started as HoopZone, a general basketball scores site, and was reworked around the Knicks. It runs on mock data, so it's a design and layout piece rather than a live feed.

title: Chat with Ashar's bot
summary: A personal chatbot that answers questions about me, my work and my background.
notes: Generated with AI. It's a SvelteKit app that knows about my background and work, so visitors can ask it questions instead of reading a resume. It also links out to my site, GitHub and LinkedIn.

title: Ashar Things
summary: A timeline of things I've done: accomplishments, experiences and life events.
notes: Generated with AI. A React app that lays out my accomplishments, experiences and life events as a timeline, as a more personal companion to my main site.

title: New York City guide
summary: A one-page guide to New York: top attractions, the five boroughs and the city's culture.
notes: Generated with AI as a single HTML page with no dependencies.

title: FIFA World Cup
summary: The history of the World Cup: every tournament, every winner and the key stats.
notes: Generated with AI around the 2026 World Cup, with sections for history, past winners and stats.

title: French Flashcards
summary: Forty everyday French words on flip cards. Mark each one Got it or Again, and missed words come back a few cards later.
notes: Made as a Claude artifact, then moved here as the first site hosted inside this portfolio. One HTML file: tap a card to flip it, and words you miss get shuffled back in a few cards later. Arrow keys work too.

title: Habitarie
summary: A habit tracker and calorie counter in one page: log food against a daily goal and check off habits day by day.
notes: Generated with AI as a single-page app with no backend: a daily calorie goal with protein, carbs and fat, a food log, and a habit checklist.

title: Birthday party invitation
summary: A playful invitation page for a birthday party, with the event details and an RSVP form. Sample event.
notes: Generated with AI as a reusable template: swap in the name, date and venue and it's ready to send.

title: AI agent registry
summary: Twenty-three ready-made agent definitions, from code review and debugging to research, writing and travel planning, for use as subagents.
notes: Each agent is one Markdown file describing its role, scope and approach, with a guide on how to plug them into an AI coding tool as focused subagents.

title: Islam knowledge base
summary: A structured reference on Islam in seventeen chapters: beliefs, the five pillars, the Quran, hadith, history, law, theology, ethics, finance and culture.
notes: Organized as numbered chapters with an index guide and suggested learning paths, so it reads like a course rather than a pile of notes.

title: Finance knowledge base
summary: Notes on personal finance, investing and markets, and company analysis, plus a map of authoritative sources and dated market snapshots.
notes: Set up so AI tools can work in it: an agent guide sets the conventions, a source map says where facts should come from, and market snapshots are dated so they never pass as current.

title: Missing Semester notes
summary: MIT's Missing Semester course, covering the shell, editors, version control, debugging and more, organized as context for AI tools.
notes: The 2019 and 2020 course materials gathered into one indexed repo, so an AI assistant can draw on them when I'm learning or working at the command line.

title: MIT Intro to CS notes
summary: Study notes for MIT 6.0001/6.0002, Intro to CS in Python: every session summarized, with deep dives on object-oriented programming and an OOP study guide.
notes: Built from MIT OpenCourseWare's Fall 2016 lecture materials and published on Santai Hub. It has a course index, detailed notes on classes and inheritance, a summary of the other sessions from recursion to Big O and sorting, and learning paths for starting from scratch or brushing up on OOP.

title: NFL knowledge base
summary: A primer on the National Football League: how the league works, the rules of the game, the teams and divisions, and the Super Bowl.
notes: Four notes published on Santai Hub as a base an AI assistant can draw on: a league overview, rules and gameplay, teams and divisions, and Super Bowl history.

title: Daily celebrations post
summary: Every morning, a Slack post lists the day's national and informal days, like National Pancake Day, so the team has something fun to start with.
notes: A scheduled Claude task looks up today's observances, picks the good ones, and posts a short formatted message to a Slack channel.

title: Food Finds
summary: A weekly digest of 15 new food spots, worldwide, around New York and Long Island, and near the office, each with a Google Maps link.
notes: Claude researches newly opened or buzzing spots, confirms each one is open and checks halal status, then rotates the focus by region each week so the list stays fresh. Every pick comes with a Google Maps link I can save in one tap.

title: NYC AI events digest
summary: A weekly email of free AI and tech events in New York over the next three weeks, plus the Luma and Partiful invites in my inbox and a few good public social picks.
notes: Claude checks Luma, Meetup, Eventbrite and other listings, keeps only free, in-person NYC events with confirmed dates, pulls my invites from Gmail, and skips anything it already sent last week. It only reads and sends one email; it never RSVPs.

title: Daily News Update
summary: Every morning, the latest world news is compiled into an organized email digest covering politics, business, technology and breaking news.
notes: Built and published as a workflow on Santai Hub, where others can download and run it for themselves.

title: Inbox labeling
summary: Each night, yesterday's new email gets sorted into labels like Promotions, Newsletters, Career and Finance, based on who sent it.
notes: Claude only labels; it never archives, deletes or marks anything read. Senders that don't clearly fit a category stay unlabeled and show up in the run summary, so I can tune the categories over time.

title: Google Drive tidy-up
summary: A weekly pass that finds 5 to 10 misplaced or badly named files in my Drive and proposes where they should go.
notes: It works through the catch-all folders first and proposes moves and renames as a numbered list. Nothing moves until I reply with which items to approve, then Claude carries them out in the same session.

title: Obsidian vault cleanup
summary: Every week, new web clippings in my Obsidian vault get filed into topic folders, renamed, titled and tagged.
notes: Claude works on the vault on my Mac using a fixed set of topic folders and a shared tag vocabulary. Moves never overwrite anything, duplicates are only flagged, and every run leaves a dated log in the vault.

title: Screenshot renamer
summary: Untitled work screenshots get descriptive names like 2026-09-11_slack-devbot-pr-reviewer-roster.png, based on what's actually in them.
notes: Claude opens each screenshot to see what's on screen, then renames it to match the folder's existing naming style. Renames go through a safe placeholder first, since macOS screenshot names hide a special space character that breaks naive scripts.

title: Bookmark review
summary: Once a month, a review of my Chrome bookmarks that finds duplicates and suggests a cleaner folder structure.
notes: If my latest bookmarks export is recent, Claude parses it with a script, normalizes URLs to catch near-duplicates, and proposes specific restructures. If the export is stale, it just reminds me to export. It never changes anything itself.

title: Meeting notes backup
summary: On the first of each month, last month's Granola meeting notes, summaries and transcripts are copied into Google Drive, one doc per meeting.
notes: Each month gets its own folder, and Claude skips meetings already saved in the previous month's backup since the 30-day windows overlap.

title: Recruiter reply drafts
summary: Polite reply drafts for recruiter emails, waiting in Gmail for me to review and send.
notes: Claude finds recruiter outreach, skips threads I've already answered or drafted, and writes a reply from my template. It only creates drafts, never sends. LinkedIn messages it can't reply to get listed separately.

title: Web mentions check
summary: A weekly scan of news and the web for new mentions of me, summarized with links.
notes: Claude searches the past week, confirms each result is actually about me rather than someone with the same name, and puts uncertain ones in a separate section. If nothing turned up, the report is one line.

title: Slack to Calendar sync
summary: Turns event posts in a Slack channel into Google Calendar events, without duplicates, and updates them when the post changes.
notes: The tricky part was making it duplicate-safe and update-aware: each event keeps a link back to its Slack message, so a re-run edits the existing event instead of adding a second one.

title: This portfolio
summary: The page you're on. Every project is one entry in a JSON file, so adding something new takes a minute.
notes: Plain HTML, CSS and a little JavaScript, no build step. Claude designed and wrote it; I add projects by editing projects.json and pushing.
